lines.text: Lending pools freeze: when borrowers take everything, depositors cannot withdraw, sometimes for days.
Exeunt is the exit market for frozen lending pools, on Arbitrum and Robinhood Chain.
Depositors sell their receipt at a discount and get paid immediately, without taking any liquidity out of the pool.
A frozen pool has no cash left, but its borrowers owe the same asset, so they are the natural buyers.
In one transaction, Exeunt takes a flash loan, repays a borrower's debt, uses that new liquidity to redeem the seller's receipt, and returns the loan.
The seller is paid, the borrower repays at a discount, and the pool is exactly as liquid as before.
Everything else is escrow, and nobody runs it: no owner, no admin, no upgrades.
This is real. In April 2026, Aave's ETH pool on Arbitrum held 148 thousand ETH, almost none of it withdrawable, for more than a day.
lines.say: This is real. In April, twenty twenty-six, Aave's ETH pool on Arbitrum held a hundred and forty-eight thousand ETH, almost none of it withdrawable, for more than a day.

lines.text: On Robinhood Earn, the USDG vault holds over half a billion dollars; less than a tenth could be withdrawn at once.
Waiting is the only built-in exit, and borrowers whose collateral is frozen are trapped too.
Exeunt turns a frozen receipt into something people want to buy.
Six things set Exeunt apart. One: the exit does not drain the pool; Exeunt creates the liquidity it uses.
Two: borrowers repay for less. At a 5% discount, 100 of debt costs 95.
lines.say: Two: borrowers repay for less. At a five percent discount, a hundred of debt costs ninety-five.

lines.text: Three: no cash needed. In flash mode, the buyer pays with collateral released by the repayment.
Four: ordinary wallets and one normal transaction.
Five: buyers are ready before the crisis, with escrowed bids and the Exeunt Vault.
Six: exit capacity is a public good, readable on-chain by anyone.
Sellers run a Dutch auction whose discount only rises, or sell now into escrowed bids.
Borrowers buy and repay in one transaction, with cash, or in flash mode, where their health factor only goes up.
Buyers who don't borrow post escrowed limit bids ahead of any freeze.
The Exeunt Vault pools capital, bids by fixed rules, and earns the discount for its depositors.
Exit capacity is published on-chain, with alerts before a freeze.
Aave borrowers can even repay with frozen collateral.
An SDK and an MCP server bring it all to apps and AI agents, without holding keys.
For Arbitrum, that means safer lending markets, where a freeze no longer has to become a bank run.
It brings the same exit to Robinhood Chain, with Paxos USDG as the main payment asset, and public risk data for curators and AI agents.
It serves depositors and loopers who need out, borrowers repaying below face value, treasuries and market makers, vault depositors, curators and AI agents.
Built in Solidity on Aave and Morpho, with Chainlink prices, a TypeScript SDK, an MCP server and a React app, it runs on Arbitrum Sepolia and Robinhood Chain Testnet.
Exeunt. The exit market for frozen lending pools.
